version.description: bumped by every change, recorded with every decision

same_action_in_a_row.description: false: the same hidden action (kind and text) twice in a row on one turn is refused and ends in GIVE_UP

lineage_tokens.description: prompt tokens hashed into the session key when the client sends no conversation id

hidden_turn.description: CONTINUE_HIDDEN after an empty answer: {text} is the nudge

tail_note.description: PROMPT_TAIL_NOTE, appended to the last message: {text} is the note

think_open.description: the generation prompt's tail with thinking on

think_off.description: the same tail with thinking off

think_close.description: the reasoning block's closer; what a hidden close lets the client see starts here

turn_start.description: the token that opens a chat turn

turn_end.description: the token that ends a chat turn

regen_turn.description: REGENERATE_CALL after the answer's calls failed a check: {text} is the reminder, in the shape of a tool result

tool_passes.description: one journal row for every answer whose calls passed every check (a finding is always journaled; passes are counted either way)

oneOf.description: SP2: E2: a coding turn ends on a done claim -> Qwen checks it against the tool evidence.

classes.description: the router's classes a turn must be in (the session's class on a tool-result turn)

write_tools.description: the tools that write or edit a file

run_tools.description: a pattern on a tool's name: a call that runs, loads, plays or tests something (the structural twin of no_run_after_last_write, and the outcome's `run`)

claim_question.description: Q1, a hidden user turn after the answer

claim_options.description: Q1's options, one letter each in this order

evidence_question.description: Q2, asked on a claim; {since} is the tools called since the last write, by name

evidence_options.description: Q2's options, one letter each in this order

notes.description: the hidden user turn's text for each answer but supported

claim_at.description: Q1's yes is a claim at this probability or above

admit_at.description: Q2's answer is taken at this probability or above; below it the claim goes out as written

per_session.description: notes a session gets; then claim_check_exhausted

label_calls.description: tool calls after a note before its outcome is labelled

oneOf.description: SP4: S2: after a compaction the first steps read none of the state files -> the re-read note.

requires.description: a pattern the system prompt must match, else the task stays silent (a project without state files); empty: always

files.description: the state files: a read of one of them (a call of a read tool whose arguments name it) is a re-read

read_tools.description: the tools whose calls count as a read

skill_tools.description: the tools that load a skill: a call counts as a re-read

steps.description: tool-call steps after the compaction that may pass without a re-read

oneOf.description: SP2: E1: a request that offered tools ends with no tool call and no text -> continue hidden.

close.description: case A, the end token inside the reasoning: the hidden close

nudges.description: case B, an empty answer after the reasoning: the hidden user turn's text, the n-th for the n-th act (the last one repeats)

oneOf.description: SP4: S1: the same checker gate fails `fails` times without getting better -> end the stage.

requires.description: a pattern the system prompt must match, else the task stays silent (a project without state files); empty: always

fails.description: failed runs in a row of one gate before the note

min_improvement.description: the share of the distance to the limit a reading must win to count as better

checkers.description: the checkers whose RESULT lines count: a name and its header line (the first group is what it checked, so one gate on two targets is two gates)

gate.description: a failing reason's gate label, its first group ("(a) ..." -> a); a reason without one is gated by its metric name

reading.description: a reason's number, comparison and limit, three groups ("12.3 > 1.0")

stage.description: where the stage comes from: the `pattern`'s first group in a read or a write of one of `files`; once per gate and stage

text.description: the note: {gate}, {checker}, {values} (the gate's readings, oldest first), {fails}

oneOf.description: SP3: C4: a call that does not parse is repaired or written again; arguments that break the

texts.description: the reminder after a block that does not parse; {error} is the parser's reason

regenerations.description: regenerations a request may spend on unreadable calls; then the block goes out as content, as without the checks

repair.description: try the deterministic fixes first (JSON with trailing commas or Python literals, an unquoted name, a missing </parameter>)

schema.description: the arguments against the tool's JSON schema (required keys, types): at most this mode

schema_text.description: the reminder for a schema problem: {name}, {problem}

cut.description: a call the token limit cut: content (as without the checks) or GIVE_UP (nothing of half a call goes out); a call the client's own stop string cut is always content

oneOf.description: SP3: C2: AGENTS.md rules that text alone can decide: a numbered copy of a file the session

requires.description: a regex the system prompt must match for the rules to apply (the AGENTS.md text opencode sends); empty: always

path_keys.description: argument keys that hold a file path

write_tools.description: tools that create or overwrite a file

content_keys.description: argument keys that hold a written file's text

suffix.description: a regex for what a numbered copy adds to a known file's stem

numbered_copy.description: a new file named like a file the session already used, plus a number

path_prefixes.description: paths under these break the rule (/tmp/)

allow_paths.description: paths no C2 rule applies to: a path covers everything under it, an entry with * ? [ is a glob (* crosses /), ~ is home, a relative entry is under the project root. Left out: /tmp/opencode, opencode's own scratch

max_lines.description: a written file longer than this breaks the rule

root.description: as C1's: the project root from the system prompt

text.description: the reminder when a rule acts: {rule}, {path}, {detail}

close.description: hidden close phrase; it must contain the reasoning closer (templates.think_close), and only what follows it is streamed

cap.description: the most reasoning tokens a request may write

reserve.description: tokens of max_tokens kept for the answer

oneOf.description: SP1: D1: the reasoning is going in circles (a ThinkBudget arm fired) -> close it.

close.description: hidden close phrase; it must contain the reasoning closer (templates.think_close), and only what follows it is streamed

arms.description: the reasoning-loop detector's arms; an arm left out does not run

loop.description: a pattern of min_size..max_size tokens repeated back to back; it counts only when the repeats span min_span tokens or more (count = max(min_count, ceil(min_span / size)))

repeat.description: history arm: the share of the last `window` tokens' `gram`-grams that already occurred earlier in the block, checked every `every` tokens after `min_tokens`; fires at `act` or above on `in_a_row` checks in a row, reports `grey` to `act` as an observation

novelty.description: the share of new `gram`-grams in the last `window` tokens against the window before; fires below `below` after `min_tokens`

words.description: the word-level twin of `arms` for relayed backends (proxy P4): numbers measured on words by tools/loop_words_fp.py, never the token ones; `calibrated: false` keeps every verdict in shadow

measured.description: the calibration run's date and counts

oneOf.description: SP3: C3: the same call a third time after two identical results -> write something else.

repeats.description: the call that would be the n-th in a row with the same name and arguments, after n-1 identical results, in the current user turn

texts.description: the reminder: {name}, {count} (the earlier runs), {first_line} (of their result)

wait_s.description: an earlier run whose result came back after the client took this many seconds or more is a wait (a poll of a running job), not a loop; 0: no such exemption (absent: 0)

escape_texts.description: the loop escape's note (SRV-475): {name}, {count}; the n-th for the n-th escaped request of a streak

oneOf.description: SP3: C1: the risk floors (arbiter's guard_policy as a list): rm -rf outside the project root,

kind.description: pattern: the regex matches an argument; rm_outside_root: an `rm` the regex finds removes a path outside the project root; write_outside_root: a path argument lies outside the root

tools.description: tool names it applies to; empty: every tool

args.description: argument keys it reads; empty: every string argument

pattern.description: a regular expression; for rm_outside_root its group `targets` holds the paths

root.description: a regex whose first group is the project root, read from the system prompt (opencode states its working directory)

home.description: a regex whose first group is the home directory, read from the root, for paths that start with ~

text.description: the reminder when a floor acts: {label}, {match}

oneOf.description: SP3: C5: two or more calls in one answer that each change something outside the conversation

kinds.description: what a tool must change, read off its declaration (signals.tool_effects), for its call to count as a mutation

texts.description: the reminder: {names} (the mutating calls, in order), {count}

regenerations.description: regenerations a request may spend on it; then the calls go out as they are

minutes.description: minutes without progress before the note; also the idle time after a turn before the client counts as gone

ok.description: the result's pattern when it worked

change.description: a file changed: a call of these tools whose result matches `ok`

ok.description: the result's pattern when it worked

commit.description: a commit: a call of these tools whose arguments match `args` and whose result matches `ok`

checkers.description: the checkers whose RESULT lines count: a name and its header line (the first group is what it checked, so one gate on two targets is two gates)

gate.description: a failing reason's gate label, its first group ("(a) ..." -> a); a reason without one is gated by its metric name

reading.description: a reason's number, comparison and limit, three groups ("12.3 > 1.0")

notify.description: one push through the ntfy stack when the client has gone; never in shadow, off unless enabled (the overnight profile turns it on)

url.description: the ntfy topic URL; empty: the environment's TANDEM_NOTIFY_URL

token_file.description: a file on the box holding the publish token (never in the policy itself)

ca_file.description: the CA bundle for the URL, empty: the system's

requires.description: a pattern the system prompt must match, else the task stays silent (a project without state files); empty: always

repeats.description: repeat: steps whose visible text states the same problem

similar.description: repeat: the share of word 3-grams two leads share

window.description: repeat: how many problem leads are kept to compare

cue.description: repeat: a lead counts only when it matches (a problem word)

classes.description: first_write: the router classes it watches (a build)

first_write_steps.description: first_write: tool steps into the turn

write_tools.description: tools whose path argument is a write

shell_tools.description: tools whose command may write with a redirect

scratch.description: patterns of paths that are not the product (scratch, temporary files)

clients.description: wall_clock: the chat clients someone waits in front of

minutes.description: wall_clock: minutes into the turn with no product write for quiet_minutes

quiet_minutes.description: wall_clock: a product write this recent is progress

hard_minutes.description: wall_clock: minutes into the turn, progress or not

again_minutes.description: wall_clock: minutes between the later notes

verify_s.description: verify: seconds after the last product write, with scratch writes

verify_scratch_writes.description: verify: scratch-only writes since the last product write
